anf_compare.notes: No PD English exists. 1 Tim 2:1, Lukan/OT quotations, Rom 8:26, Matt 11:25 follow familiar wording.

apparatus: §1 invisible-God sentence very rough; §3 Moses-Deut bridge rough; Daniel/Tobit aside rough; Esther fragments broken.

choices.why: The four 1 Tim 2:1 names with ascending frankness (parrhesia); 'petition' for deesis (needy's asking), 'intercession' for enteuxis (bold face-to-face).
Parrhesia = free-spokenness before God; grades petition→prayer→intercession.

choices.english: hearing such is intercession — if we hear names more strictly
choices.term: ἀκούειν τοιαύτην ἐστὶν ἔντευξις, εἰ τὰ ὀνόματα κυριώτερον ἀκούοιμεν
choices.why: Origen's strict-name hermeneutic: even 'he said' (Joshua/Samson) counts as enteuxis when names are heard strictly.

choices.english: the son, or myself, or whomsoever
choices.term: τὸν υἱὸν ἢ ἐμὲ αὐτὸν ἢ ὃν δή ποτε
choices.why: The epileptic father's open alternative kept open.

pass_a_gloss: Benefits expounded, examine the agraphon (ask great/heavenly; small/earthly added): visibles are symbols/types, intelligibles true (rough invisible-God sentence); converse with saints through prayer imitates them, asking the same heavenly-great things they typically asked, earthly-small supplied by need's measure (Father knows beforehand, Matt 6:8). Four names for four things (1 Tim 2:1): deesis = needy's asking for lacking things; proseuche = nobler doxological asking for greater; enteuxis = bolder asking from greater frankness; eucharistia = confessing thanksgiving for benefits/magnitude. Examples: 1st — Gabriel/Zechariah (Luke 1:13); Moses calf (Exod 32:11) + fasts/Deut 9:18 (rough bridge); Mordecai/Esther (fragments). 2nd — Azariah (Dan 3); Tobit (Tob 3:1-2); Daniel unknown (Song obelized); Tobit/Judith rejected by circumcision-party (rough) → Habakkuk (Hab 3:1-2), Hannah, Jonah (Jon 2:2-4). 3rd — Spirit intercedes (Rom 8:26-27; double verb kept); Joshua's sun (Josh 10:12-13) counts as enteuxis under strict names; Samson (Judg 16:30). Rule: deesis/enteuxis/eucharistia to holy men too (Paul/Peter; even wronged non-saints); much more thank/intercede to Christ (Stephen Acts 7:60; epileptic father Matt 17:15 open alternative; Lord's 'I confess/thank You' Matt 11:25).
